articles.title: Hackers Used Meta’s AI Support Bot to Seize Instagram Accounts
articles.summary: Microsoft just dropped a record-breaking 200 security patches in one Patch Tuesday because apparently their code quality control is having an existential crisis. Nearly three dozen earned the coveted 'critical' rating—because why fix things right the first time when you can fix them dramatically later?

articles.title: Congress Just Rushed Through a Disastrous Copyright Office Overhaul
articles.summary: A CISA contractor accidentally published AWS GovCloud keys and agency secrets on GitHub like it's their personal diary, prompting Congress to demand answers. Nothing says 'cybersecurity leadership' like your own contractor leaking your crown jewels on the world's most public code repository.

articles.title: Enshittification Merch That Actually Fights Enshittification
articles.summary: Section 702 FISA mass surveillance authority faces its biggest challenge yet as Congress finally grows a spine about warrant requirements. The stakes have never been higher for telling the surveillance state to get a damn warrant like the Constitution actually matters.

articles.title: Scott Pelley Shows How Legacy Media Got It Wrong — Before Bari Weiss Made It Worse
articles.summary: Nightmare-Eclipse drops another Windows Defender zero-day called RoguePlanet, continuing their beautiful feud with Microsoft's security team. When a researcher goes full scorched earth against Redmond, we all win—except for Windows users, obviously.

articles.title: Top Pentagon Official Admits Boat Strike May Have Killed Victims of Human Trafficking
articles.summary: Senator Ron Wyden reports unprecedented bipartisan support for reining in domestic spying laws, which is either a miracle or the apocalypse. After decades of being the lone voice screaming about surveillance overreach, Wyden finally has company in the 'maybe mass spying is bad' camp.

articles.title: GitHub pulls pin on npm's auto-run scripts
articles.summary: An angry researcher with a Microsoft grudge drops another Windows zero-day because revenge truly is a dish best served with working exploit code. Nothing motivates vulnerability research quite like corporate spite and a functioning GitHub account.

articles.title: CISA Adds Cisco, Chrome, and Arista Flaws to KEV Catalog Amid Active Exploitation
articles.summary: CVE-2026-5027 in Langflow is being actively exploited for unauthenticated RCE, because apparently AI platforms are just as terrible at security as everything else. Pro tip: maybe patch your AI tools before the bots become sentient AND compromised.

articles.title: Chaotic Eclipse Unveils RoguePlanet Exploit Targeting Fully Patched Windows
articles.summary: Microsoft patches YellowKey, GreenPlasma, and MiniPlasma zero-days that grant SYSTEM privileges and BitLocker bypass capabilities. The rainbow of exploit names suggests either a very creative researcher or someone who really loves colorful ways to own Windows boxes.

articles.title: France probes compromise of gov messaging platform after account hijack
articles.summary: France's 'sovereign' encrypted messenger Tchap got breached, with officials and the attacker hilariously disagreeing on how badly they got owned. Building your own WhatsApp to avoid trusting Big Tech only works if you can actually secure the damn thing.

articles.title: Netherlands Seizes 800 Servers, Arrests 2 for Aiding Cyberattacks
articles.summary: Hackers used Meta's AI support bot to hijack Instagram accounts including Obama's White House and US Space Force profiles, defacing them with pro-Iranian content. When your AI chatbot becomes the weakest link in account security, maybe it's time to reconsider the whole 'AI for everything' strategy.
